title: Full Rows
story: Singers stand on risers that branch like a tree: one singer at the top, and under each singer a place on the left and a place on the right, each taken or empty. Read the places row by row from the top, each row from left to right. The choir is tidy when, once you meet an empty place, no singer comes after it, in that row or in any row below. Is the choir tidy? An empty stage is tidy.

notes: The numbers on the singers do not matter, only which places are taken.

hints: Reading row by row is what a queue of nodes does: DEQUEUE a singer, look at the LEFT place and then the RIGHT place, and ENQUEUE the singers you find there.
Keep one yes/no variable: has an empty place been seen yet? It starts as no and never goes back, not even when a new row begins.

For each of the two places: IF it IS NOT NOTHING, then IF an empty place was seen before RETURN no, otherwise ENQUEUE it; ELSE remember that an empty place has been seen. When the queue runs out, RETURN yes.
edgeCases: a right place taken beside an empty left place
an empty place in the middle of the last row
a singer in a lower row after an empty place
